description: Known pain pathways. Used by the rules layer to link pains that appear in connected regions within a time window, and to constrain AI output. Region IDs refer to data/body-atlas.json. Structure IDs refer to the stock anatomy model; '{s}' is replaced with the matched side (l/r).

side_rules.same_side: Both pains must be on the same side (a centre-line region matches either side).
side_rules.any_side: Pains can be on either side.

pathways.name: Lower back → buttock / back of leg
pathways.plain_explanation: The sciatic nerve is formed from nerve roots in your lower back and runs through the buttock and down the back of the leg. Irritation near the spine is often felt further down the nerve.
pathways.specialist: Physical therapist or sports-medicine / spine doctor

pathways.name: Lower back / SI joint → groin
pathways.plain_explanation: Nerves that leave the upper lumbar spine (ilioinguinal, genitofemoral, femoral) supply the groin and front of the thigh, and the psoas muscle connects the lumbar spine to the inner hip. The SI joint also commonly refers pain to the groin.
common_contributors: Lumbar disc or spinal joint irritation
Tight or overloaded psoas / hip flexors

pathways.name: Hip joint → groin, front of thigh, knee
pathways.plain_explanation: The hip joint shares nerve supply (obturator and femoral nerves) with the groin, front of the thigh and the knee, so hip problems are often felt lower down, sometimes only at the knee.
common_contributors: Hip joint irritation or early wear
pathways.specialist: Sports-medicine doctor, orthopaedist or physical therapist

pathways.name: Kidney → flank → groin
pathways.plain_explanation: Pain from the kidney or ureter (for example a kidney stone) is felt in the flank and often travels down toward the groin as the problem moves. Fever or urinary symptoms with this pattern need prompt medical care.

pathways.name: Jaw joint (TMJ) ↔ neck, ear, temple
pathways.plain_explanation: Your jaw muscle (masseter), temple muscle (temporalis) and the neck muscles that attach just behind your ear work as one chain. Clenching or a forward-head posture loads all of them, so pain often travels between the jaw, ear, temple and neck.
common_contributors: Clenching or grinding, often at night or during heavy lifts

pathways.name: Neck → shoulder, arm, hand
pathways.plain_explanation: Nerve roots leaving the neck form the brachial plexus, which supplies the shoulder, arm and hand. Irritation in the neck can be felt anywhere along that path, often with tingling or numbness.

pathways.name: Upper trapezius / neck → head (tension-type headache)
pathways.plain_explanation: Tight upper trapezius and neck muscles refer pain up the back of the head to the temple and behind the eye. This is one of the most common drivers of tension-type headaches.

pathways.name: Gallbladder → right shoulder blade
pathways.plain_explanation: The gallbladder sits under the right ribs. Irritation there is often felt under the right shoulder blade, typically after a fatty meal.

pathways.name: Diaphragm → shoulder tip
pathways.plain_explanation: The diaphragm is supplied by the phrenic nerve, which comes from the same neck roots (C3–C5) as the skin over the shoulder tip, so irritation under the diaphragm is often felt at the top of the shoulder.
common_contributors: Irritation below the diaphragm (e.g. gallbladder, spleen)

pathways.name: Heart → left arm, jaw, neck, back
pathways.plain_explanation: Heart pain is often felt in the chest and can spread to the left arm, jaw, neck or upper back. This pattern always needs urgent medical assessment.
common_contributors: Reduced blood flow to the heart

pathways.name: Foot arch / heel ↔ calf
pathways.plain_explanation: The calf muscles, Achilles tendon and plantar fascia work as one continuous chain. Tight calves load the heel and arch, and foot pain changes how the calf works.
common_contributors: Sudden increase in running or standing

pathways.name: Hip / glute weakness → knee
pathways.plain_explanation: When the glutes don't control the hip well, the thigh rotates inward and the knee takes extra load, commonly felt at the front or outside of the knee.

pathways.name: Forward-head posture → neck, upper back, jaw, headache
pathways.plain_explanation: When the head sits forward of the shoulders, the neck and upper-back muscles hold far more load, and the jaw position shifts. This often shows up as neck, upper-back and jaw pain plus headaches.
